messages:
deploy-bot: [CI] Release candidate v2.3.1: image push to registry failed -> 403 Forbidden. image=redwood/api:2.3.1-candidate sha=sha256:abc123
raj: ugh. which step exactly? build succeeded?
sylvia: build passed, push step errored out — logs show `denied: requested access to the resource is denied`
ci-agent: uploading artifact to registry-stage.redwood.internal:443 -> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden. token appears to be rejected.
maya: likely the deploy token rotated yesterday. who owns the registry token? @oncall-ryan
oncall-ryan: I rotated prod tokens but left stage token alone. I'll check stage creds now. give me 2m
sylvia: we have canary gate blocked, deployment stuck in pipeline. release-manager-alex: we were hoping to cut prod tomorrow, this will block the rollout if unresolved.
raj: if token rotation is the culprit can we just re-run push with CI using `--username=_json_key --password-stdin` creds from vault?
ci-agent: attempted re-run with vault creds failed — vault lookup returned 403 as well. suspect registry policy rejecting image tag from CI runner identity.
maya: note: recent registry policy change limits anonymous/wildcard pushes from ephemeral runners. need explicit repository write permission.
release-manager-alex: two options: 1) pause the release and pin to older image for tomorrow's window, 2) emergency change to registry policy (risky). Thoughts?
raj: prefer pause and pin. policy change could open writes to wrong org.
ci-agent: quick mitigation: we can manually push the image from a long-lived service account that has write perms. command we used locally: 
```
docker login registry-stage.redwood.internal -u sa-release-bot -p $TOKEN
docker push redwood/api:2.3.1-candidate
```
But that needs the service account token pulled from KMS and run from approved host.
sylvia: that manual push would get the canary deployed, but doesn't solve CI runners failing — ops will still need a fix.
release-manager-alex: OK. plan: run manual push to unblock the canary for tonight's smoke tests, and pin the release job to image `redwood/api:2.3.0` for the scheduled prod window until registry policy is rolled back or CI identity fixed.
oncall-ryan: I have the SA token. I'll perform the manual push and post proof. after that I'll open a ticket with infra to audit registry ACLs and rotate the CI service principal permissions.
maya: add action: update release notes with a footnote about image pin and that v2.3.1 will be retried after infra fix.
raj: also add a CI job to validate registry write perms before build push step (fast check) so we fail earlier with clearer errors.
release-manager-alex: noted. alex created release blocker ticket #RI-4721 and assigned to infra. tagging: @infra, @security for registry ACL review.
oncall-ryan: manual push done: pushed redwood/api:2.3.1-candidate from sa-release-bot at 1768456842. canary pipeline resumed. logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/17684/logs
sylvia: canary passed smoke tests. promoting to canary-traffic.
release-manager-alex: thanks all. keeping release paused for prod pin until infra confirms fix. I'll update the release calendar. :thumbsup:
raj: follow-up: include rollout rollback playbook link in ticket.
ci-agent: created CI PR to perform pre-push registry-write check -> https://git.internal/redwood/ci/pulls/859
maya: closing loop: will re-run full pipeline after infra confirms perm fix, target next nightly for v2.3.1 retry.
release-manager-alex: last note: document ephemeral runner permissions in runbooks. we almost relied on manual SA carryover.
raj: agreed. thanks everyone.
